366	we mentioned that the error of the spies was
367	in a very, very high place. It was not a simple error.
368	We spoke about this point: it was not
369	simply that they came and spread a bad report about the Land. Rather,
370	the yetzer hara succeeded in misleading the spies
371	on a level so subtle and so high, that they understood
372	and believed that it was truly not yet time to enter the Land of
373	Israel, not yet time to enter the Land of
374	Israel. One more generation had to be spent in the desert. And that
375	is the Parashah of last week. In this week's Parashah,
376	Parashat Korach, we see how the concealment and the error
377	grow greater and greater. The spies
378	did not intend to rebel against Moshe Rabenu's leadership. They
379	did not intend to disqualify Moshe Rabenu. They accepted
380	Moshe Rabenu. They said: Moshe, you are a tzaddik, but on one
381	point you are mistaken, to enter the Land of Israel now. You are
382	mistaken. Humble yourself toward us, understand that you are very great,
383	you are in abundant light, you go on in such greatness.
384	Understand, we are not yet able, we are not yet
385	ready to enter the Land of Israel. In this the spies erred.
386	They did not deny all of Moshe Rabenu's leadership,
387	but it was already a cruder, sharper error
388	than the error of Miriam, and it keeps developing.
389	And now in the Parashah of this coming Shabbat we
390	see how it reaches
391	the deed of Korach, where Korach already comes to Moshe Rabenu
392	and says: you are a liar, you are not a true leader.
393	He said: you saw so many things, you saw
394	what Moshe Rabenu did for the people of Israel, the ten plagues and the whole
395	Exodus from Egypt, the splitting of the Red Sea, all the miracles. Moshe
396	Rabenu, you say he is a liar? What does Korach say?
397	Korach says: yes, he was a true leader, he fell,
398	he failed. And what does Korach think, that Moshe Rabenu failed?
399	Rabenu HaAri says that Korach said: Moshe Rabenu intended
400	his pride in being a leader has already corrupted him.
401	From now on he no longer speaks to us true words.
402	That's it, he was a true leader, he failed and he fell. What was the error of
403	Korach? Where did Korach err? As we mentioned last week,
404	that we should not think the error of the spies was simple, one must
405	know that the error of Korach was not simple either.
406	Korach was, as we mentioned a few months ago,
407	in the Holy Zohar on Parashat Tazria, the Zohar says: there is
408	none greater in all the tribe of Levi than Korach. Korach
409	was the greatest in the whole tribe of Levi. That is to say,
410	he was a very, very great man, Korach, and he was
411	a master of attainment, wisdom and Ruach HaKodesh at a very,
412	very high place, and even in that high place Korach made
413	a very great error, to the point that he rebelled against all
414	the leadership of Moshe Rabenu. And Moshe Rabenu knows
415	that the moment there is, among the people of Israel, a dispute
416	against the tzaddik, the true leader whom HaShem
417	appointed, there is no greater damage than this. There is
418	no damage that can be greater
419	than beginning to dispute the true leader. Why?
420	Because if we dispute the true leader, who
421	reveals to us what HaShem wants? Who reveals
422	to us in fact His will and the mind of HaShem? The tzaddik and the leader. If we
423	deny, if we go out against the true tzaddik and leader,
424	we are already cutting ourselves off, not
425	from the tzaddik, we are cutting ourselves off from HaShem,
426	and then that is already the greatest danger.
427	Therefore we see that Moshe
428	Rabenu, with all the sins and transgressions there were among the people of Israel
429	in the desert, we see the sin of the Golden Calf, which our Sages say
430	what a grave sin that was, that at Mount Sinai,
431	the place where they had just heard "I am HaShem your Elokim," they made a molten
432	calf, "You shall have no other gods before Me," at Mount
433	Sinai, in the same place, 40 days after saying
434	the Ten Commandments that idolatry is forbidden, there
435	in that same place they commit idolatry. What could be
436	graver than that? Moshe Rabenu hears that there is a decree
437	against the people of Israel. What does he say to HaShem?
438	"And if not, blot me out of Your book." If You do not forgive them, blot me out of Your book.
439	"If You forgive their sin, and if not, blot me out of Your book." He goes
440	with self-sacrifice to the very end
441	for the people of Israel. Also in the sin of the spies we
442	see everywhere that Moshe Rabenu
443	prays immense and awesome prayers for the people of
444	Israel. In Korach's dispute, what does Moshe Rabenu do?
445	Moshe Rabenu at first tries to appease them, that they do
446	teshuvah, that they return. When they do not repent, what
447	does Moshe Rabenu say? "If these die as all men die, then
448	I am a liar." He says to HaShem: create for them a special
449	grave, that the earth open its mouth, which had never
450	happened before, and swallow Korach and all his congregation. Where
451	are Moshe Rabenu's kindnesses, where is Moshe Rabenu's
452	compassion? Only, it is written in all the commentators that Moshe Rabenu
453	knew: if they dispute me, if they come to me and do not
454	accept,
455	they in fact deny my leadership, it is not my issue.
456	I did not want to be a leader, Moshe Rabenu says.
457	What did I want? I did not take even one donkey from them. Did I
458	ever want to be a leader? I took nothing from them.
459	But the moment they deny my leadership, there is
460	the greatest disaster among the people of Israel, because it creates
461	the separation, the disconnection between the people of Israel and HaShem.
462	And this leadership is for all generations,
463	for all generations until the coming of Mashiach
464	Tzidkenu, and so the mind and the will of
465	HaShem is revealed and reaches us through the tzaddik.
466	And therefore the moment a person has an error, the moment a person
467	disputes the tzaddik, he is in fact cutting himself off
468	from HaShem. Therefore Moshe Rabenu behaved
469	in such a way toward Korach and his congregation. But if
470	we ask a question, where did Korach's own error
471	come from? What was Korach's error? What was the wrong?
472	Rashi brings the words of our Sages: "What did Korach see to commit this folly?"
473	Why do you come to dispute Moshe Rabenu? What do you lack?
